_readme: Department-wise budget figures for Andhra Pradesh, transcribed from the Demands for Grants volumes published by the AP Finance Department. This is the detail the platform was missing: the state-wide capital outlay total says nothing about whether the money went into school buildings or into anything else. Demand-wise it does. Every row names the volume and the column it came from. Nothing here comes from a newspaper.

how_to_read.title: How to read a demand
how_to_read.body: Andhra Pradesh's budget is voted demand by demand, forty demands, one broad department each. Demand 12 is School Education, demand 33 is Major and Medium Irrigation. The numbering is stable across every year in this collection. Each demand splits in two, but what the two halves mean changed in 2017-18. Up to 2016-17 the split was Non-Plan and Plan: committed spending against new schemes. From 2017-18 the Plan classification was abolished nationally and the split became Revenue and Capital: running costs against money that leaves behind a building, a road or a piece of equipment. Those two cuts answer different questions and are never joined into one line here. The same year appears three times as the estimate hardens: BE is the budget estimate made before the year starts, RE is the revised estimate near the end of it, and Actual is what the audited accounts finally recorded. All forty demands have BE for all thirteen years. Only School Education and Medical and Health have RE and Actual so far.
how_to_read.the_honest_limit: A budget estimate is a plan, not an outcome. A government that budgeted heavily and spent little looks identical to one that budgeted heavily and spent it all, until the audited actuals arrive. Everything labelled 'as budgeted' on this page is a plan. Where we have audited actuals we say so and show them separately, and we never add a plan to an outcome to make a total.
how_to_read.units_note: The volumes print rupees in Indian grouping, which reads oddly if you are used to plain numbers: 29963,50.62 means Rs 29,963.51 crore, and in the 2014-15 book the same style counts thousands rather than lakhs. Every figure here has been converted to crore and reconciled against the printed grand total of its own book, to the paisa, for all thirteen years.

demand_map_note: Andhra Pradesh votes forty demands, one broad department each. The numbering is stable across all thirteen years in this collection: the books number them in Roman up to 2022-23 and in Arabic from 2023-24, but demand 12 is School Education in every one of them.

rows.note: Gross. Net 25,741.51. Arithmetic checks out.

rows.page: Demand XII summary, column 'Accounts 2022-23' (printed 478,92.15 lakh gross capital)
rows.note: Gross, consistent with every other year in this series. Eye-checked against the printed page on 27 August 2026 from a reader-supplied copy of the volume. The same column deducts recoveries of Rs 501.58 crore against capital — more than the year's entire gross capital outlay — making NET capital MINUS Rs 22.66 crore. Both figures are printed on the page; the volume does not say what was recovered or why, and we do not guess. Earlier attempts to transcribe this cell produced the gross and the net as two 'contradictory' readings; they are both real.

rows.page: Demand XVI abstract, column 'Accounts 2022-23' (printed 10881,03.38 / 515,73.62 / 11396,77.00)
rows.note: Arithmetic checks out. Realised hospital capital outlay 516 cr against a 3,713 cr BE — a 14% execution rate.

rows.page: Statement of Demands for Grants 2023-24, Volume I/2, demand 16 row

rows.page: Demand XVI abstract, column 'Revised Estimate 2023-24' (printed 13540,50.99 / 1385,13.18 / 14925,64.17)
rows.note: Arithmetic checks out.

rows.page: Statement of Demands for Grants 2024-25, Volume I/2, demand 16 row

rows.page: Demand XVI abstract, column 'Revised Estimate 2024-25' (printed 14812,49.58 / 2214,15.13 / 17026,64.71)
rows.note: Arithmetic checks out. Unusually, capital was revised UP.

rows.page: Demand XVI abstract, column 'Accounts 2024-25', GROSS rows
rows.note: HIGH CONFIDENCE. NET after recoveries: Revenue 13,760.48, Capital 1,114.97, Total 14,875.45 — and those net figures match the 2026-27 Budget in Brief 'Medical' sector row (13,760.49 / 1,114.97 / 14,875.46) to the lakh, which independently confirms both the figures and the units convention. caveats.title: These are budget estimates, not spending
caveats.body: Thirteen years of BE for all forty demands come from Volume I/2 of each year's Demands for Grants. They are what the government asked the Assembly to authorise. What was actually spent is in the audited accounts, and for most demands we do not have it yet.

caveats.title: The Plan/Non-Plan break at 2017-18
caveats.body: Charts that show Revenue against Capital start at 2017-18. Before that the books did not publish that split at all; they published Plan against Non-Plan. A chart running a Revenue line back to 2014-15 would be inventing data, so this one stops where the data stops.

caveats.title: Governments served different lengths
caveats.body: The 2014 government had five budgets, the 2019 government five, and the government from 2024 has three so far. Compare the yearly figure, not the total across a tenure.

caveats.title: A zero in the orders count is usually a missing department, not an idle one
caveats.body: Secretariat departments are created, merged and renamed. Tribal Welfare shows no orders before 2019 because it did not exist as a separate department then; its work sat inside Social Welfare. Grama/Ward Sachivalayams exists only under the 2019 government and Swarna Gramam only under the present one. Read a zero as 'this department did not exist', unless the department clearly did.

caveats.title: One secretariat department can administer several demands
caveats.body: Panchayat Raj and Rural Development is one department but two demands; Water Resources covers both Major and Medium Irrigation and Minor Irrigation. Where that happens the same order count appears against each demand and must not be added together. Each entry says so.

caveats.title: The orders register cannot be totalled for money
caveats.body: Every order carries an amount column, and on most orders it is zero or blank even when the order itself states a figure in its subject line. Counting those zeros as spending would understate some departments by tens of thousands of crore. This platform counts orders as decisions and takes every rupee figure from the budget books and the audit reports instead.
